title: IntentIR V1
description: Conversational Intent Intermediate Representation. Records what the user wants, including incomplete, preferred, excluded, and deictic information. Not an execution plan, capability, or recipe.

schema_version.description: Intent IR language version. V1 documents are always "1.0".

intent_id.description: Stable identity of this intent. Later turns reuse the same id; they do not mint a new schema or a new intent.

revision.description: Monotonic snapshot number of this intent_id. Each conversational update writes a new revision of the same intent.

source_text.description: Latest utterance that produced this revision. Optional. Never a substitute for structured fields.

action.description: The verb. Absent when the utterance does not name one. Unresolved when the verb is known to be missing.

object.description: The primary entity the action applies to. May stay unresolved ("this", "that one", "her").

target.description: App, channel, or provider (WhatsApp, YouTube, Emirates as carrier target). Distinct from object.

domain.description: Optional coarse domain. Never required. Leave absent rather than guessing.

slots.description: Named extra fields (when, place, destination, content, ordinal, …). The extension point for V1 — new meaning is a new slot name, not a new top-level field.

preferences.description: Soft wants that must not be collapsed into resolved slots ("I'd prefer Emirates").

exclusions.description: Hard nos that must not be dropped ("Nothing overnight").

name.description: Required on slots[]. Omitted on action/object/target/domain (name is implicit).

value.description: Resolved content. Null when status is unresolved. Never invent a value to satisfy the schema.

status.description: resolved = known value; unresolved = known gap; ambiguous = competing candidates, no winner.

candidates.description: Competing values when status is ambiguous.

path.description: Dimension being constrained (airline, tone, schedule, cuisine, price, …). Not a JSON Pointer.

value.description: The preferred or excluded value. Preferences do not resolve slots; exclusions do not delete slots.
